arc: The teaching traces the upward ladder by which the dispersed elements of the natural are gathered inward, each to its higher kindred, until the whole ascends in one motion through the Pillar of Glory, the First Man, and the Ambassador into the aeons of the Greatness — the place of rest forever.
reading:
This chapter is titled "Concerning the Gathering-Inward," and it answers a single question: in what manner do the elements gather inward, one to another? The whole teaching is the description of a vertical chain of conjunction, in which every level of being returns to its own at the level immediately above it, until the entire series has risen as one motion into the inmost.

The argument begins at the lowest degree of natural substance. Fire gathers to the fire of the fire — that is, the natural love-power gathers to its own purer principle higher up — and likewise wind gathers to the wind of its higher kindred. This is the law of correspondence applied as a ladder: like gathers to like, but always to a more interior like. What is dispersed in the cosmos as fire, wind, water, and the rest is being drawn home through its own essential quality, each element finding its own purer source one degree above. This is the redemptive reversal of the original scattering of the Five Sons of the First Man into matter; every grain of the Living Soul travels back along the same line by which it descended.

Above the bare elements the chain rises through three named stations of the regenerative process: Tamr, Answer, and Call. The order is decisive and must be read upward in the direction of cause. The Call (ⲡⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ) is the summons of Divine Truth originating above; the Answer (ⲡⲟⲩⲱϣⲃⲉ) is the soul's Hearing that returns the call upward; and the Tamr (the ordered fruit-cluster of refined natural states) is what the elements first compact into when they begin to ascend. So the elements gather to the Tamr, the Tamr to the Answer, the Answer to the Call. The natural is conjoined to the receptive response, and the response is conjoined to the summons that first awakened it. The whole regenerative dialogue is here being collected into its own source.

From the Call the ascent passes into the rational and celestial degrees. The Call gathers to the chosen Mind, which the text identifies as the Noeric — illumined rational understanding, the Mind of Light awakened in the regenerate. The Noeric in turn gathers to the Pillar of Glory, the column of accumulated truth that is the very road of ascent. The Pillar gathers to the First Man, Divine Truth in his redemptive descent, who is also the gatherer of all that he originally sent down. The First Man gathers to the Ambassador, the revealing call of Divine Truth in the inmost. And the Ambassador gathers to the aeons of the Greatness — the celestial fullness of the Father.

The teaching then makes its decisive structural point: all of this gathers "at one and the same time." The chain is not a slow ladder climbed rung by rung in succession; it is a single simultaneous conjunction in which every degree, the moment it is taken up at its level, is already taken up at every higher level, because the whole series moves as one organism. This is how regeneration actually works in the doctrine of correspondences: when the lowest natural is rightly conjoined, the whole column from element through faculty through Pillar through First Man through Ambassador stands conjoined with it, and the soul ascends through all the discrete degrees in one motion. They go up "to the upper place, to the place of rest, forever and ever."

What the teaching describes, then, is the architecture of the soul's homecoming. Every element, every faculty, every divine emanation is paired with its corresponding higher principle, and the whole chain is the inverse of the original dispersal. The natural fire returns through the rational fire to the divine love; the natural wind returns through perception to the breath of the Spirit; the answering soul returns through the Call into the Mind of Light; the Mind of Light rises by the Pillar of Glory, which itself is held open by the First Man, who is sustained by the Ambassador, who stands in the aeons of the Father. To gather inward is therefore to be conjoined upward, and the doctrine here is that this conjunction, when it is real at any one rung, is real at every rung at once, and brings the soul into eternal rest.
title: The Ladder of Gathering-Inward: How the Elements Ascend as One into the Greatness
